concepts.name: Geological Origin and Structural Composition of Andaman & Nicobar Islands
key_dimensions: Tectonic origin: submerged continuation of Arakan Yoma fold mountains (Myanmar), NOT a volcanic arc in entirety
Role of Indo-Australian Plate subduction under Eurasian Plate in island formation
Presence of the only active volcano in India — Barren Island — and dormant Narcondam Island
Distinction between sedimentary, volcanic, and coral components within the same island group

concepts.name: Geological Origin and Structural Composition of Lakshadweep Islands
key_dimensions: Coral atoll formation: built on submerged volcanic peaks, NOT continental shelf extensions
Distinction between atolls, lagoons, and reefs in the Lakshadweep context
Comparison with Andaman & Nicobar: coral vs. fold mountain origin — a classic UPSC trap
Role of the Chagos-Lakshadweep Ridge as the submarine foundation

concepts.name: Barren Island and Narcondam: India's Volcanic Islands
key_dimensions: Barren Island: only active volcano in India AND the only active volcano in South Asia
Narcondam Island: dormant (not extinct) stratovolcano — distinction matters
Location of both within Andaman Sea, administratively part of Andaman & Nicobar UT
Recent eruption history of Barren Island and its ecological implications (UPSC GS1 + Environment overlap)

concepts.name: Indira Point: India's Southernmost Tip
key_dimensions: Located on Great Nicobar Island — NOT on mainland India
Submergence during 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami: geomorphological and strategic significance
Proximity to the Strait of Malacca and its strategic/maritime importance
Confusion trap: often mistaken for Port Blair or Car Nicobar as the southernmost point

concepts.name: Ten Degree Channel and Nine Degree Channel: Maritime Separators
key_dimensions: Ten Degree Channel: separates Andaman Islands from Nicobar Islands (not two separate countries)
Nine Degree Channel: separates Lakshadweep (Minicoy Island) from the main Lakshadweep group
Eight Degree Channel: separates Minicoy from Maldives — frequently confused with Nine Degree Channel
Strategic importance of these channels for naval navigation and India's maritime doctrine

concepts.name: Duncan Passage and Preparis Channel
key_dimensions: Duncan Passage: separates South Andaman from Little Andaman Island
Preparis Channel: separates North Andaman from Myanmar's Preparis Island — international boundary significance
Coco Channel: separates North Andaman from Coco Islands (Myanmar) — strategic concern regarding Chinese presence
UPSC trap: confusion between Duncan Passage, Ten Degree Channel, and Coco Channel locations

concepts.name: Administrative and Geographic Structure of Andaman & Nicobar Islands
key_dimensions: Total islands: ~572, but only ~37 are inhabited — distinction between total and inhabited count
Three main island groups: Andaman (North, Middle, South), Little Andaman, and Nicobar group
Car Nicobar: northernmost of the Nicobar group and site of a key Indian Air Force base
Great Nicobar: southernmost and largest of Nicobar Islands, site of proposed holistic development project

concepts.name: Administrative and Geographic Structure of Lakshadweep
key_dimensions: Smallest Union Territory of India by area (~32 sq km) — frequently tested
36 islands total, of which only 10 are inhabited — a common numerical trap
Three groups: Aminidivi Islands (northernmost), Laccadive Islands (central), Minicoy Island (southernmost, culturally distinct)
Minicoy's cultural uniqueness: closer to Maldivian culture, speaks Mahl language — NOT the same as mainland Kerala

concepts.name: Coral Reef Ecosystems and Lagoons of Lakshadweep
key_dimensions: Lakshadweep: one of India's three major coral reef regions (others: Gulf of Mannar, Andaman & Nicobar)
Atoll structure: coral reef surrounds a central lagoon — geomorphological process of formation
Coral bleaching threats due to rising sea surface temperatures: UPSC Environment overlap
Agatti Island: only island in Lakshadweep with an airport — strategic and tourism angle

concepts.name: Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and Strategic Maritime Significance of Island Territories
key_dimensions: Islands dramatically expand India's EEZ: Andaman & Nicobar contributes ~30% of India's total EEZ
UNCLOS provisions: island vs. rock distinction for EEZ entitlement — conceptual clarity needed
Andaman & Nicobar's position astride the Strait of Malacca: monitoring of global shipping lanes
Lakshadweep's EEZ in the Arabian Sea: strategic importance vis-à-vis Pakistan and Chinese naval presence

concepts.name: Climate of Andaman & Nicobar Islands
key_dimensions: Tropical rainforest climate: no dry season, high humidity year-round — NOT the same as monsoon climate
Receives both Southwest and Northeast monsoon — a rare geographic distinction among Indian regions
Great Nicobar receives among the highest rainfall in India — often tested in ranking questions
Cyclone vulnerability: located in the Bay of Bengal cyclone belt — 2004 Tsunami impact context

concepts.name: Climate of Lakshadweep Islands
key_dimensions: Tropical maritime climate: moderated by surrounding ocean, less extreme than continental India
Receives Southwest monsoon only (NOT Northeast monsoon) — contrast with Andaman & Nicobar
Low annual rainfall despite being surrounded by sea: paradox explained by limited orographic lift
Vulnerability to sea-level rise: average elevation less than 2 meters — existential threat angle

concepts.name: Tribal Populations and Protected Area Regime of Andaman & Nicobar
key_dimensions: Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs): Sentinelese, Onge, Jarawa, Andamanese, Shompen, Nicobarese
North Sentinel Island: protected under Andaman & Nicobar Islands (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Act — no contact policy
Jarawa Tribal Reserve and the Andaman Trunk Road controversy: infrastructure vs. tribal rights
Shompen of Great Nicobar: threatened by the proposed Great Nicobar holistic development project

concepts.name: Great Nicobar Island: Biodiversity and Strategic Development Project
key_dimensions: Biosphere Reserve status: includes Galathea Bay Wildlife Sanctuary and Campbell Bay National Park
Leatherback sea turtle nesting site at Galathea Bay: critically threatened by proposed port development
Holistic Development Project: transshipment port, international airport, township — NITI Aayog proposal
Geopolitical rationale: countering China's String of Pearls strategy and Hambantota Port influence

concepts.name: Vegetation and Biodiversity of Andaman & Nicobar Islands
key_dimensions: Tropical evergreen and tropical semi-evergreen forests dominate: high endemism rate
Andaman Padauk (Pterocarpus dalbergioides): commercially valuable endemic timber species
Marine biodiversity: dugongs, saltwater crocodiles, leatherback turtles — Schedule I species
Islands are part of the Indo-Burma Biodiversity Hotspot — UPSC Environment overlap

concepts.name: Vegetation and Marine Ecology of Lakshadweep
key_dimensions: Coconut palm dominates: economic backbone (copra production), shapes cultural identity
Mangrove absence is notable: unlike Andaman & Nicobar, Lakshadweep has negligible mangrove cover
Sea grass beds and coral reefs support unique marine food webs including sea turtles and reef fish
Lakshadweep designated as a Ramsar Wetland candidate — conservation policy dimension

concepts.name: Soil Types and Land Characteristics of the Island Groups
key_dimensions: Andaman & Nicobar: laterite and alluvial soils in valleys — supports tropical agriculture
Lakshadweep: sandy, calcareous (coral-derived) soils — low fertility, limits agricultural diversity
Lakshadweep's soil salinity issue: freshwater lens beneath islands is thin and vulnerable to contamination
Comparison trap: Andaman soils support paddy and spices; Lakshadweep soils primarily support coconut

concepts.name: Tsunamis, Seismicity, and Natural Disaster Vulnerability
key_dimensions: Andaman & Nicobar lies on the highly seismic Alpide Belt / Pacific Ring of Fire adjacency — Zone V seismicity
2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami: catastrophic impact, submergence of Indira Point, reshaping of coastlines
Lakshadweep is NOT seismically active but is vulnerable to tsunamis generated in the Indian Ocean
Post-2004 reforms: Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre (ITEWC) established at INCOIS, Hyderabad

concepts.name: Minicoy Island: The Geographical and Cultural Outlier of Lakshadweep
key_dimensions: Separated from main Lakshadweep group by the Nine Degree Channel — geographic isolation
Culturally aligned with Maldives: Mahl-speaking population, matrilineal society
Administratively part of Lakshadweep UT despite geographic and cultural distinctiveness — a UPSC trap
Strategic location: close to international shipping lanes in the Arabian Sea

concepts.name: Freshwater Resources and Water Security of Island Groups
key_dimensions: Lakshadweep: entirely dependent on rainwater and thin freshwater lenses (Ghyben-Herzberg lens) beneath coral islands
Sea-level rise and over-extraction threaten saltwater intrusion into freshwater lenses — climate-security nexus
Andaman & Nicobar: rivers and streams exist (e.g., Galathea River on Great Nicobar) — unlike Lakshadweep
Comparison trap: Andaman has surface freshwater; Lakshadweep has no rivers or lakes — only groundwater lenses
